sections.label: The work
sections.statement: Forty years between the catalyst <t>and the reactor.</t>
body: Thirty-seven years at ExxonMobil Chemical in Baytown, Texas: eleven as Chief Scientist of global R&D, seven as Chief Polymer Science Advisor. Research that helped carry metallocene catalysis from the laboratory bench into world-scale reactors, and the products built on it: films, packaging, elastomers, adhesives, engine-oil additives and the separator membranes inside lithium-ion batteries.

Since 2019, an independent practice in polyolefins: consulting, expert testimony in patent matters, research with the University of Houston and Baylor University, and a company of his own, Molecular Joinery, for composite design and coupling chemistry.

sections.label: The defining chapter
sections.title: Metallocenes, <t>at world scale.</t>
sections.body: A new family of catalysts promised polyethylenes with properties the old chemistry could not reach. The work at ExxonMobil Chemical took them from the bench to supported catalysts running in gas-phase reactors, and into the products built on them. Two decades on, the same discipline produced the separator membranes inside lithium-ion batteries.
